concepts.name: Classes and objects
concepts.summary: Explain that a class defines a template of data and behaviour and that objects are individual instances created from it.

concepts.name: Attributes and methods
concepts.summary: Identify attributes as the data an object holds and methods as the operations it can perform.

concepts.name: Constructors and initialisation
concepts.summary: Describe how a constructor sets an object's initial state when it is created.

concepts.name: Object state and identity
concepts.summary: Understand that each object has its own state and that two objects with equal data are still distinct objects.

concepts.name: Calling methods on objects
concepts.summary: Explain that using an object means invoking its methods, which read or change its state.

concepts.name: Self reference
concepts.summary: Understand that this or self refers to the current object inside its methods.

misconceptions.text: A class and an object are the same thing.
Two objects with the same attribute values are the same object.
Changing an attribute in one object changes it in every object of that class.

concepts.name: Encapsulation and access control
concepts.summary: Apply private fields and public methods so that an object's state is changed only through a controlled interface.

concepts.name: Getters, setters and validation
concepts.summary: Write accessors and mutators that enforce rules on state instead of exposing raw fields.

concepts.name: Inheritance and subclassing
concepts.summary: Create a subclass that reuses and extends a superclass's attributes and methods.

concepts.name: Method overriding
concepts.summary: Override an inherited method in a subclass and call the superclass version when needed.

concepts.name: Basic polymorphism
concepts.summary: Use a superclass-typed reference to call methods whose behaviour depends on the actual object type.

concepts.name: Class-level members
concepts.summary: Distinguish data and methods that belong to the class from those that belong to each instance.

concepts.name: Composition between objects
concepts.summary: Build objects that hold references to other objects and delegate work to them.

misconceptions.text: Making fields private is only about hiding them and does not protect the object's consistency.
Inheritance is the best way to reuse any code.
Overriding a method and overloading a method are the same thing.

concepts.name: Abstract classes and interfaces
concepts.summary: Define abstract types that specify behaviour without implementation and implement them in concrete classes.

concepts.name: Dynamic dispatch
concepts.summary: Analyse how the method executed is chosen at runtime from the object's actual class.

concepts.name: Composition over inheritance
concepts.summary: Compare inheritance and composition for a design and choose based on coupling and flexibility.

concepts.name: Liskov substitution principle
concepts.summary: Analyse whether a subclass can stand in for its superclass without breaking the expectations of callers.

concepts.name: Responsibility-driven class design
concepts.summary: Decompose a problem into classes with focused responsibilities and high cohesion.

concepts.name: Coupling and dependencies
concepts.summary: Analyse how dependencies between classes affect changeability and reduce them through abstractions.

concepts.name: Object relationships in UML
concepts.summary: Model classes and their associations, aggregations and inheritance in class diagrams.

concepts.name: Equality, copying and immutability
concepts.summary: Distinguish identity from value equality, shallow from deep copies, and know when to make objects immutable.

misconceptions.text: An interface is just an abstract class with no code, so the two are interchangeable.
If a subclass compiles and overrides all methods, it is a valid substitute for its parent.
Deep inheritance hierarchies show good object-oriented design.

concepts.name: SOLID principles in tension
concepts.summary: Evaluate a design against the SOLID principles and judge where applying one conflicts with another or with simplicity.

concepts.name: Creational design patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse when factory, builder or singleton patterns solve object-creation problems and what costs they bring.

concepts.name: Behavioural design patterns
concepts.summary: Select and apply strategy, observer or template method to vary behaviour without altering clients.

concepts.name: Structural design patterns
concepts.summary: Use adapter, decorator or facade to compose and integrate objects while keeping interfaces stable.

concepts.name: Dependency injection and inversion
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs that depend on abstractions supplied from outside to improve testability and flexibility.

concepts.name: Refactoring toward better design
concepts.summary: Diagnose design smells such as god classes and feature envy and judge refactorings that fix them.

concepts.name: Designing for testability
concepts.summary: Structure classes so collaborators can be replaced by test doubles and behaviour verified in isolation.

misconceptions.text: Design patterns should be applied wherever possible because they make any design better.
A singleton is a harmless way to share global access to an object.
Following every SOLID principle maximally always yields the best design.

concepts.name: Fit of object-oriented paradigm
concepts.summary: Judge when an object-oriented approach suits a problem compared with functional, procedural or data-oriented styles.

concepts.name: Domain-driven object modelling
concepts.summary: Create a rich domain model with entities, value objects and aggregates that express business rules and invariants.

concepts.name: Designing extensible frameworks
concepts.summary: Design class hierarchies and interfaces for libraries that third parties can extend without breaking them.

concepts.name: Evolving hierarchies and compatibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate how changes to base classes and public interfaces ripple to subclasses and clients, and plan safe evolution.

concepts.name: Object design under concurrency
concepts.summary: Evaluate object designs for shared mutable state hazards and choose immutability, confinement or synchronisation.

concepts.name: Architectural use of objects
concepts.summary: Create system architectures that place object boundaries and dependencies to isolate domain logic from infrastructure.

concepts.name: Anemic versus rich models
concepts.summary: Critique designs that separate data from behaviour and justify where each style is appropriate.

misconceptions.text: Object-oriented design is always the right choice for large systems.
Modelling every real-world noun as a class produces a good domain model.
Wrapping fields in getters and setters makes an object safe to share between threads.
